explanation: In running prose this pole fires on the words that pick out a person or a counted set of referents whose identity is left open: the personal pronouns he/she/they/you, the relative and possessive who/whose/their, the indefinite person words people/everyone, the strong quantifiers both/many/multiple/numerous, and the focus particle 'only'. It fires on those words whatever the grammatical role is (clause subject, predicate complement, or object of a preposition), so it is a referent-class detector rather than a positional one, and it sits at its floor on definite already-identified reference (the + noun, clerk/man, him/her/them/his/its, it/this/that/which, things), on copulas and auxiliaries (is/was/are/be/been/will/would), and on technical or code nouns; in a fixed slot the same sentence reads about 0.4 of max higher with 'They' than with 'It' and about 0.25 higher with 'people' than with 'things'.
